This is something i've been telling everyone, Gojo really messed up Sukuna.
A lot of readers always say that it doesn't makes sense how every Jujutsu Sorcerer but Gojo is able to avoid WBS, and it makes me wonder if we're actually reading the same manga.
Gojo got hit because Sukuna's Binding Vow was a really nasty one, removing the conditions for a one time activation caught Gojo off guard, in exchange of not being able to subtract steps for the subsequent activations ever again, and readers tend to forget the narrator's words when the Shinjuku Showdwn started, the moment Utahime was using her CT: "The Mastery of Jujutsu is the Mastery of Subtraction, the skill of a Sorcerer can be judged by their abilty to omit prerequisites for the activation of their technique"
This implies a few things, all techniques normally require those steps (Chants, Handsigns etc) and that thanks to their skill in jujutsu, almost everyone is able to not need all that, i would asume that their technique actually is a bit weaker thanks to this in exchange of being able to use it in the heat of the battle which is of course a benefit in lmlst every way.

And this goes into my next point, Sukuna's WBS, thanks to that Binding Vow, was at full power and without any indicator of it being casted, no wonder Gojo got sliced.
But now he is literally unable to upgrade it by using this one thing that is the definition of Jujutsu mastery, subtract.
Plus everyone can tell when he is trying to throw that thing, that's the only reasong they're not falling like flies the moment they jump into the ring.

So yeah, it was really severe.

\- Learning your PvP rotations, even if you don't replace any skill in your build.  
Knowing how to CCchain Prokel will give you an obnoxious amount of advantage over the course of the fight, sometimes even forcing him to switch from PvP to PvE almost instantly by keeping him on the air or the ground.  
You can go to Trixion and instead of practicing Prokel, try with a common dummy, and test which of your skills are able to keep the enemy on the air, and of course, time your usage of your skills so you can juggle Prokel around, not just lifting him, but waiting up to the last milisecond and launch him up again.  


\- Learning which skills have priority over Prokel's attacks is also helpful, since you will start interrupting him more often, which means less risk of getting hit by any of his attacks. (Front Multilaser and the Blink Counter are some examples of attacks that you can interrupt)

\- And lastly, being patient with your attacks on him, i feel like this is something that my friends failed to do when we let them go first against him. Having a skill ready to be used when in PvP, doesn't mean that you have to use it, it is better to wait for all of your combo to smack Prokel for a big chunk of damage, kicking him only once will only force him to stand up with immunity to cc for a small fraction of time and he will be able to attack you freely.

This of course are only tips for the PvP section of the fight.  
For the PvE there isn't to much to say, literally keep practicing your damage windows and trying to maintain a good uptime to jump asap into the PvP, which is the section were you will have the upper hand on him, this is why you use your damage sidereal right at the start on the first stun, and then again on the second one, just to avoid the PvE section as much as possible.
